newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia's return to WTO a priority - institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia's return to WTO a priority - institute.

text.p: Yugoslav membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) is one of the most strategic corridors for its reintegration in world markets, the Belgrade Institute of Economic Sciences said on Monday.

Yugoslavia's membership in the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, the forerunner to the WTO, was suspended in 1992 along with other international organisations, when the U.N. imposed sanctions for Belgrade's role in the war in Bosnia.
But last Tuesday, the U.N. voted to end sanctions, clearing the way for Yugoslavia to begin talks about resuming suspended memberships.

"Now that sanctions have been lifted, Yugoslavia must engage more in regulating its status in the WTO," Mladjen Kovacevic told a presentation of the institute's latest publication 'Yugoslavia and the WTO'.
Kovacevic said neither the Yugoslav nor the republican governments of Serbia and Montenegro had dealt seriously enough with the problem.
Other analysts insisted returning to the WTO would not solve the country's economic problems alone.
A professor at the Belgrade University's School of Political Sciences, Vujo Vukmirica argued major restructuring was necessary.
"We face a bitter struggle to return to previous positions. But the question is where will others be by then," he said.
Vukmirica said maximum efforts had to be exerted in liberalisation of the economy, especially of foreign trade.

The Belgrade University's School of Economics head Miomir Jaksic said a return to world markets is top priority for a small economy like Yugoslavia's which must export half its GDP. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
